questions.q: What happened to Middletown, Ohio after its steel manufacturer was outsourced?
a: Jobs disappeared, home values fell and residents stayed poor
New technology companies moved in and raised wages
The town quickly recovered through farming and tourism
Most families relocated to nearby cities for better schools
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the lost steel jobs and falling property values trapped many residents in poverty.

questions.q: What were the three rules Vance's grandmother set for him?
a: Earn good grades, hold a job and help at home
Attend church, play sports and save money
Finish homework, cook dinner and watch his siblings
Stay out of trouble, study math and find an apprenticeship
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists Mamaw's rules as earning good grades, holding a job and helping her around the house.

questions.q: What does Vance say he learned during his time in the Marines?
a: How to care for himself, lead others and manage money
How to study efficiently and pass difficult exams
How to network with wealthy and influential people
How to repair engines and work with his hands
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the Marines taught him self-care, leadership and financial management.

questions.q: What two things does Vance credit for helping him beat the odds?
a: Hard work and social capital
Natural intelligence and family wealth
Scholarships and athletic talent
Luck and a supportive neighborhood
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Vance believes hard work plus knowing the right people allowed him to succeed.

questions.q: What are adverse childhood experiences linked to, according to the studies in the summary?
a: Weaker school performance, depression, anxiety and heart disease
Stronger resilience and better problem-solving later in life
Higher income once the person enters the workforce
Greater willingness to seek help from teachers and doctors
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites research connecting childhood adversity with poorer grades and higher risks of mental and physical illness.
